The win probability surface is derived from play-level descriptors such as down, distance, yard line, and scoring events, forming a conditional probability distribution over game outcomes. The isomorphism layer bridges schema inconsistencies among data providers, allowing unified access to player and game state information. Failure modes include unmatched names, missing roster entries, and incomplete game data prior to kickoff. These primitives form a closed-loop system where player identity enables accurate game state modeling, which in turn supports real-time inference of strategic decisions.
